mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes Vito 108-113 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Vito 108-113 CDI engine replacement typically costs between £1,100 and £2,900 depending on engine code (OM611 or OM646), condition type, and whether fitting is included. Rebuilt OM611 (W638, 1996-2003): £1,100-£2,500 supply only. Rebuilt OM646 (W639, 2003-2010): £1,100-£2,900 supply only. Used engines from breakers: £450-£1,100 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,200 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common failure on the Vito OM646 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM646's single-row timing chain gradually elongates under sustained high-load commercial use, typically between 100,000-140,000 miles. Cold start rattle is the earliest warning sign of chain elongation. Crankshaft position sensor fault codes often appear before complete failure. Ignoring the noise risks chain jump causing catastrophic valve and piston interference. Rebuilt OM646 units include upgraded timing components to prevent recurrence.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM611 cylinder head cracking in a W638 Vito?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM611's aluminium cylinder head can develop cracks near the injector bores, particularly on high-mileage W638 examples. Loss of compression and hard starting. Diesel pooling in the valve cover around injectors. White smoke from the exhaust. Coolant loss with no visible external leak. Cracks longer than 7mm require cylinder head replacement.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my Vito 108-113 CDI engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner on OM646, injector seat repair on OM611, EGR cooler). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. OM646 timing chain replacement: £1,500-£2,200 - do this if rattle is constant. OM611 injector seat repair: £400-£700 - effective for cracks under 7mm. Full OM646 rebuild: £1,800-£3,200 - for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles. Full OM611 rebuild: £1,400-£2,200 - for catastrophic failure or 150k+ miles. Given Vito 108-113 CDI values (£2,500-£6,000), evaluate repair vs replacement carefully.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my Vito 108-113 CDI has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block near the injector pump. W638 Vito (1996-2003): OM611.981. W639 Vito (2003-2010) 109 CDI: OM646.983. W639 Vito (2003-2010) 111 CDI: OM646.980. Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used Vito 108-113 CDI engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a Vito diesel. The W638 and W639 subframe geometry and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Subframe must be lowered - not a driveway job. Injection pump timing requires precise calibration tools. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation required. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,200 - worth every penny.

milestones.description: W638 Vito launched with OM611 2.2L common-rail diesel, 82-122hp, cast-iron block
W639 Vito launched with OM646 2.2L diesel (refined OM611 architecture), 87-150hp
OM646 gains Euro IV emissions compliance with EGR cooler and DPF
W639 facelift introduces OM651 engine, OM646 phased out in 113 CDI and above

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Vito 108-113 CDI (Older) Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Vito 108-113 CDI range relies on the OM611 and OM646 2.2-litre diesel families - robust commercial workhorses that have developed well-documented reputations for specific, predictable failures. Timing chain elongation dominates OM646 replacement demand, while OM611 cylinder head cracking near injector bores is a known failure mode on high-mileage W638 examples. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common Vito 108-113 CDI engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM646 Timing Chain Elongation - Why the Vito 111 CDI Rattles and Loses Timing
problems.rootCause: The OM646's single-row timing chain gradually elongates under sustained high-load commercial use, overwhelming the hydraulic tensioner and causing misalignment that risks catastrophic interference failure. Crankshaft position sensor fault codes often appear before complete failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Front-access chain replacement with upgraded tensioner and hardened guide rails
repairOptions.longevity: Restores timing accuracy; only recommended before interference or cam damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt engine with reinforced timing components, supply & fit, dyno tested
repairOptions.longevity: Resolves elongation and secondary bottom-end wear; best long-term value for older chassis

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W639 Vito 109-111 CDI is worth £2,500-£6,000 depending on condition and mileage - the full replacement cost of £1,800-£3,200 often approaches vehicle value. For vehicles worth under £3,000, evaluate repair options carefully.
problems.recommendation: For a Mercedes Vito W639 approaching high mileage, preventative chain replacement often exceeds the vehicle's residual commercial value. We advise a full rebuilt OM646 swap once rattle is constant at idle or if fault logs show timing deviation, as it eliminates recurring tensioner faults and restores full payload reliability without hidden ancillary costs.
problems.cta: -> Compare OM646 Mercedes Vito 108-113 CDI replacement costs

problems.h4: OM611 Cylinder Head Cracking - Why the W638 Vito 108-110 CDI Loses Compression
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Vito 108 CDI, 109 CDI, 110 CDI (W638, 1996-2003, OM611.981)
problems.rootCause: The OM611's aluminium cylinder head can develop cracks near the injector bores, particularly if injector hold-down bolts have been over-tightened. Injector seat erosion also causes compression loss and hard starting.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Machine injector seats, fit new hold-down bolts and copper washers
Replace cylinder head with refurbished unit, new injectors, gaskets, bolts
repairOptions.longevity: Required if cracks exceed 7mm or multiple bores affected

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt OM611 with new cylinder head, injectors, timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required for catastrophic failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W638 Vito 108-110 CDI is worth £1,500-£4,000 - the full replacement cost of £1,400-£2,200 often approaches or exceeds vehicle value. Evaluate carefully.
problems.recommendation: If you suspect cylinder head cracking on your W638 Vito, have the injector bores inspected immediately. Injector seat repair at £400-£700 is effective if cracks are under 7mm. On a high-mileage W638 Vito with multiple bore cracks, a full rebuilt OM611 is often the only reliable solution to prevent repeat failure.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM611 Mercedes Vito 108-113 CDI replacement engines

problems.group: OM646 Injector Seal & EGR Cooler Failure
problems.h4: OM646 Injector Seal & EGR Cooler Failure - Carbon and Coolant Loss on W639 Vito
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Vito 109 CDI, 111 CDI (W639, 2003-2010, OM646 family)
problems.rootCause: Degrading injector copper seals allow combustion gases into the crankcase, carbonising pistons and oil rings. Simultaneously, the EGR cooler develops thermal micro-cracks, mixing coolant with exhaust gases and reducing combustion efficiency.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Injector Seals & EGR Cooler Swap
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Seal replacement, upgraded cooler installation, engine oil flush to remove sludge
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before ring damage or severe overheating; stops progression

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete supply & fit, updated seals, tested EGR/coolant systems, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Guaranteed resolution; eliminates hidden cylinder wall scoring and turbo contamination

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a W639 Vito worth £2,500-£6,000, injector seal and EGR replacement at £800-£1,400 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if compression loss or bottom-end damage is present.
problems.recommendation: We recommend a full reconditioned engine if compression drops significantly or if coolant contamination has already damaged turbocharger bearings. Partial fixes on a heavily carbon-damaged OM646 rarely survive commercial delivery cycles, making a complete rebuilt unit the most cost-effective long-term investment for fleet operators.
